profile.headline: Alaska's governor is courting data centers to create demand for North Slope gas, while most public comment and one senator push back.

sections.text: Gov. Mike Dunleavy has been recruiting data centers to raise energy demand and justify a gas pipeline. In January 2026 he was working with DigitalBridge, majority owner of Switch, and released an independent WilmerHale review of the state's $75 million commitment to a DigitalBridge fund. A bill requiring data centers to pay their own grid costs died in committee in May 2026.

Stak Energy has proposed a $500 million data center on about one square mile of state land near the Dalton Highway on the North Slope. It could eventually need 1 to 3 GW of self-generated power from North Slope gas, with construction planned from summer 2026 and operations by late 2028 (May 2026). The Pentagon has offered about 4,700 acres near Anchorage, Healy and Fairbanks for up to a dozen military data centers.

Public comments on the state's proposed 50-year lease for the North Slope project were mostly opposed; fewer than a dozen supported it (July 2026). The Fairbanks North Star Borough Assembly discussed a data center moratorium in 2026.

Sen. Lisa Murkowski (R) said she is "not a proponent of data centers" at JBER or Interior military installations because of Alaska's insecure energy base. Sen. Dan Sullivan (R) has pushed to bring data centers onto military bases in the state. In September 2026 both senators said they were open to AI guardrails.

The University of Alaska Anchorage College of Engineering opened a Master of Science in Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, and Engineering in fall 2025 (announced June 2025), aimed at building AI models for problems such as wildfire risk and energy resilience. UAA also hosts the NSF-funded Alaska AI Solutions Consortium, which held its first meeting in June 2025. In September 2026 the Board of Regents reviewed a draft AI policy requiring all three UA universities to write AI implementation plans; a final version is targeted for the November 2026 meeting.

profile.headline: Alabama's biggest AI story is Project Marvel, a $14 billion data center in Bessemer that was approved under a nondisclosure deal residents are still fighting.

sections.text: Gov. Kay Ivey created a Generative AI Task Force by executive order in February 2024; it delivered its final report in March 2025. In February 2026 she formed a Technology Quality Assurance Board to carry out its recommendations, including use of the NIST AI Risk Management Framework in state agencies.

The Bessemer City Council approved Project Marvel, a $14 billion, 18-building hyperscale campus, in November 2025. A revised plan in February 2026 expanded the site to 1,600 acres; the project is described as a 1-gigawatt data center.

A nondisclosure agreement released in July 2026 showed Bessemer officials had been required to destroy records about Project Marvel; it came out after environmental groups threatened to sue over public records. Birmingham has considered a 270-day moratorium on data-center activity. In September 2026 a conservative anti-data-center group brought a bus tour to Bessemer and McCalla.

In April 2026 the University of Alabama moved to create a School of Data Science focused on AI, the first such academic unit in the state. It is also opening the Alabama Center for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence in its College of Engineering with a $2 million gift.

Sen. Katie Britt co-sponsored the GUARD Act in October 2025 to require age verification and bar minors from AI chatbots. On September 1, 2026 she called for public accountability from data-center developers and praised the Ratepayer Protection Pledge as "an outstanding first step". In late September 2026 she co-sponsored the bipartisan AI Systems Transparency Act. Sen. Tommy Tuberville, the Republican nominee for governor, supports expanding data centers.

profile.headline: Arkansas's governor calls data centers the largest investments in state history, while the county around Little Rock has fought over pausing them.

sections.text: Gov. Sarah Huckabee Sanders launched an AI working group in June 2024; its AI and Analytics Center of Excellence delivered recommendations and a state AI use policy in February 2026. Sanders called the $6 billion AVAIO data center in Pulaski County "the largest investment in Arkansas history" (January 2026).

Google began a $4 billion data center on 1,100 acres outside West Memphis in October 2025, to be spent through 2027 and powered in part by a new 600 MW Entergy Arkansas solar project with 350 MW of storage. AVAIO plans a $6 billion data center in Pulaski County (January 2026), and a $6.6 billion project was proposed in the Arkansas River Valley (July 2026).

Pulaski County's Quorum Court approved a one-year data-center moratorium in May 2026 with an exemption, amid opposition to the AVAIO project. In September 2026 County Judge Barry Hyde vetoed new data-center rules the court had passed. Carroll County imposed a 12-month pause on June 16, 2026, and Union County a one-year moratorium from July 10, 2026. Little Rock passed its own data-center ordinance in June 2026.

In August 2026 the University of Arkansas, Fayetteville launched the Arkansas Materials Institute, with artificial intelligence among its five research areas. In April 2026 the University of Arkansas at Pine Bluff opened a university-wide Center for Artificial Intelligence and Data Analytics.

profile.headline: Arizona is one of the top two data center markets in the world, and in 2026 it paused the tax break that drew them there.

sections.text: Gov. Katie Hobbs signed HB 4168 on June 13, 2026. It stops the Arizona Commerce Authority from accepting data center sales-tax incentive applications from July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2029. Hobbs said Arizona is in the "Top Two market in the world for data centers". Her proposed data center water-use fee was left out of the budget. In September 2026 she declined calls to pause data center development itself.

Microsoft is expanding its five-building, $1.5 billion campus in Goodyear, and in May 2026 it paid more than $131 million for 100 more acres there. Project Blue, a $3.6 billion, 290-acre data center complex near Tucson, won Arizona Corporation Commission approval (4-1) for TEP to supply its power in December 2025. Amazon later withdrew from the project.

Tucson's City Council rejected Project Blue in August 2025 over water and power; Pima County approved the land sale and rezoning, and Attorney General Kris Mayes moved to block its utility deal. On December 11, 2025, Chandler's council voted 7-0 against a $2 billion AI data center after residents sent more than 250 emails.

Arizona State University was OpenAI's first university partner, in January 2024. In September 2025 the partnership was expanded to give ChatGPT Edu with GPT-5 to every ASU student, faculty member, researcher and staff member at no cost to them.

In September 2026 Sens. Mark Kelly and Ruben Gallego and Reps. Greg Stanton, Yassamin Ansari and Adelita Grijalva (all D) asked Interior Secretary Doug Burgum about 12 data center projects proposed on more than 17,600 acres of federal land in six Western states, four of them in Arizona. Kelly's "AI for America" plan (September 2025) proposes an AI Horizon Fund, paid into by AI companies, for worker training and power and water infrastructure.

profile.headline: California wrote the first US law aimed at catastrophic risk from frontier AI, and in 2026 it began restricting the data centers that AI runs on.

sections.text: Gov. Gavin Newsom signed SB 53, the Transparency in Frontier AI Act, on September 29, 2025; it requires developers of models trained above 10^26 FLOPs to publish safety frameworks and report critical safety incidents, from January 2026. Executive Order N-5-26 (March 2026) set AI procurement standards, a May 2026 order addressed AI job disruption, and a September 18, 2026 order convened experts to report within two months on strengthening AI safety law, including a possible "kill switch" for advanced models.

The largest data center proposed in California is a $10 billion, 330-megawatt campus of nearly 1 million square feet in Imperial County, put forward by developer Sebastian Rucci (reported April 2026). In September 2026 Newsom signed seven data center laws, including SB 886 and AB 2383, which require the Public Utilities Commission to set separate power rates so data centers cover their grid costs, and a water-use disclosure rule he had vetoed in 2025.

Imperial County supervisors froze data center projects for 45 days in 2026, then extended the freeze to a year. In Santa Clara, the Planning Commission delayed a GI Partners AI data center and required more public outreach. A 2026 PPIC survey found 51% of California voters oppose building new data centers and 73% oppose one in their own community.

Stanford's Center for AI Safety, in the School of Engineering, holds its 2026 annual meeting on October 5, 2026 under the theme "Trust, Verified". At UC Berkeley, the Center for Long-Term Cybersecurity runs an AI Security Initiative on AI risk-management standards, and the Berkeley AI Research lab held its 2026 graduate showcase in July 2026.

Rep. Jay Obernolte (R) co-wrote the Great American AI Act discussion draft with Rep. Lori Trahan (D-MA), released June 4, 2026; it would bar states from regulating AI model development for three years. The draft folds in Rep. Ted Lieu's (D) AI Grand Challenges Act, and Rep. Scott Peters (D) was involved in its release. In July 2026 Lieu introduced a bipartisan AI Kill Switch Act that would require labs to report security incidents and create a way to shut down their most powerful models.

profile.headline: Colorado passed the first broad state AI-discrimination law and then scaled it back, while its Front Range cities and counties pause data centers.

sections.text: Gov. Jared Polis delayed the 2024 Colorado AI Act to June 30, 2026 (signed August 2025). On May 14, 2026 he signed SB26-189, which repeals it and replaces its "high-risk AI" rules with a narrower law on automated decision-making in consequential decisions, effective January 1, 2027. In 2026 the legislature killed both a data center tax-break bill and a bill requiring data centers to pay for their own clean power.

Vantage Data Centers' Trident project in Aurora, 334 MW of IT capacity and about 500 MW total on 143 acres across from homes, would be Colorado's largest data center and can be approved without a public hearing (September 2026). QTS Denver-Aurora (177 MW) will be Xcel's largest industrial customer. Xcel's April 2026 large-load tariff for users of 50 MW or more requires 15-year contracts and an 80% minimum demand charge.

Larimer County (January 2026), Jefferson County and Boulder County (June 2026) adopted temporary data center moratoriums. Denver approved a one-year moratorium in May 2026, Longmont banned hyperscale centers over 100 MW in June, and Broomfield paused them for 18 months in July. Earthjustice and other groups intervened against Xcel's data center tariff in 2026.

CU Boulder leads the NSF National AI Institute for Student-AI Teaming (iSAT), whose funding NSF renewed for five more years in 2025. In July 2026 CU Boulder's research office awarded more than $200,000 to nine interdisciplinary AI pilot projects.

On September 25, 2026 Sen. Michael Bennet (D) proposed the AI Regulator Act, which would create an independent federal agency to regulate frontier AI models and social media, with power to pause the release of models that pose catastrophic risk. Sen. John Hickenlooper (D), a member of the Senate Commerce Committee, wrote the bipartisan VET AI Act directing NIST to build standards for independent third-party evaluation of AI systems, and in September 2026 called for AI hearings and stronger guardrails and pressed the White House and Congress for independent third-party evaluation of the most powerful models.

Trumbull adopted a two-year moratorium on new data centers on September 9, 2026, as 365 Data Centers weighs converting a 15 MW site there for AI; Morris (two years), Groton and West Haven (one year) did the same. In September 2026 Sen. Chris Murphy warned of "AI companies in a blind race to build a death machine first" and called for binding rules.

Connecticut's data-center incentive law, signed by Gov. Ned Lamont in March 2021, waives sales, use and property taxes for 20 to 30 years for projects investing $50 million to $400 million or more. By 2026 only Cigna had used it, saving about $17 million in sales tax on its Windsor data center. A proposed 1.5-million-square-foot hyperscale data center tied to the Millstone nuclear plant in Waterford was dropped. In his 2026 State of the State address Lamont said the state had told new data centers to "slow down" unless they add generation. In September 2026 Republican candidate Ryan Fazio called for repealing the tax break.

sections.text: Starwood Digital Ventures proposed Project Washington, a 6-million-square-foot, 1.2 GW data center in Delaware City with 516 backup diesel generators.

In February 2026 DNREC ruled Project Washington barred by the Coastal Zone Act, largely over its diesel generators. New Castle County Council adopted data-center rules in March 2026, and Starwood dropped its appeal in August 2026, so the project will not proceed as planned.

On September 18, 2026 Sen. Lisa Blunt Rochester and Sen. John Curtis asked Senate Commerce Committee leaders to hold a hearing with AI company executives on the capabilities and safety of their systems.

Matt Meyer signed HB 16 amending the state AI Commission law in May 2025, and in July 2025 signed a joint resolution to develop an AI Sandbox for corporate governance, biotech, healthcare, chemicals and finance, to give "space for visionaries and risk-takers to responsibly test cutting-edge artificial intelligence technologies in Delaware." His FY26 budget included $150,000 for AI career and technical education. In March 2026 the state launched a Responsible AI training course for state employees.

The University of Delaware opened the First State AI Institute in June 2025, led by Sunita Chandrasekaran, to build open-source research tools, with Unidel Foundation funding for AI hardware. In July 2026 NSF awarded UD $21.5 million over five years to lead the NSF AI Institute for Human-AI Cooperation, directed by Cathy Wu, with Delaware State, Penn, Florida and Princeton, focused on AI in physical therapy and rehabilitation.

The governor's AI Bill of Rights (child-safety, disclosure) passed the Senate but was blocked by a House speaker who defers to federal preemption.

items.text: Asks the Tenth Judicial Circuit to bar OpenAI from developing new models without independent third-party safety approval and to block minors from ChatGPT.

items.title: SB 482 — Artificial Intelligence Bill of Rights
items.text: Passed the Senate 35-2 but the House refused to take it up in the regular session or the spring special session.

profile.headline: Florida's governor wanted state AI rules the federal government would not write; his own House passed only the data-center half, and counties are pausing projects themselves.

sections.text: Gov. Ron DeSantis proposed an "Artificial Intelligence Bill of Rights" and a data-center bill in December 2025. The Senate passed the bill of rights (SB 482, including parental consent for minors on companion chatbots), but the House blocked it, saying AI rules belong at the federal level. The data-center bill, SB 484, was the only part to survive; DeSantis signed it on May 7, 2026. It requires AI data centers to pay for their own utility costs rather than shift them to customers. DeSantis has opposed federal preemption of state AI laws.

At least 16 Florida cities and counties had adopted or were considering data-center moratoriums by August 2026. Palm Beach County advanced a one-year moratorium and rejected Project Tango, a $2.6 billion data center planned for Loxahatchee. A 15-million-square-foot hyperscale proposal in St. Lucie County (Project Jarvis) was withdrawn in February 2026. Citrus and Lake counties moved to pause data centers, Hillsborough voted unanimously to draft a moratorium, and Orange County planned one in September 2026.

The University of Florida launched the fourth generation of its HiPerGator supercomputer in October 2025, a $33 million NVIDIA DGX B200 system with 504 Blackwell GPUs, which UF calls the fastest university-owned supercomputer in the country. UF built a campus-wide AI curriculum around the machine.

Rep. Byron Donalds, described as the Republican frontrunner for governor, said in 2026 that he disagrees with President Trump on federal preemption of state AI laws, and wants states able to regulate AI use of a person's name, image and likeness and to expand parental controls. Sen. Rick Scott has sponsored the ASK Act (first filed May 2023), which would require parental consent before minors use products with AI features.

In April 2026 the Fort Meade City Commission in Polk County unanimously approved a development agreement for a $2.6 billion, 4.4-million-square-foot hyperscale data center by Stonebridge on a 1,300-acre former phosphate mine, with about $140 million in county tax breaks over 10 years and power from Duke Energy. Water use was capped at a claimed 50,000 gallons a day, pending a separate water-district permit. In May 2026 Gov. Ron DeSantis signed SB 484, the Florida Hyperscale Data Center Act, which sets a permitting framework for data centers using 50 MW or more.

states.summary: Georgia enacted SB 540 (signed 2026-05-15, effective 2027-07-01), a chatbot child-safety law enforced by the attorney general. Nothing found on frontier-model or catastrophic risk; the governor opposed the federal moratorium on state AI laws.

items.title: SB 540 — conversational AI protections for minors
items.text: Requires AI disclosure, bars sexually explicit and romantic interactions with minors, mandates crisis resources and parental controls; effective July 1, 2027.

profile.headline: Georgia is one of the country's largest data-center markets, and power bills from that boom are now an issue in the governor's race, the utility-commission race and the Senate delegation.

sections.text: Gov. Brian Kemp backs data-center growth. In July 2026 he called a blanket moratorium "irresponsible" and "insane", said he is "more concerned about China winning this race", and added "We don't need to try to push these things where people don't want them." The state runs an Office of Artificial Intelligence. In March 2026 the state Senate passed a bill to repeal data-center sales-tax exemptions early; Kemp had vetoed a pause on those exemptions in May 2024.

OpenAI plans a $20 billion data center at an industrial site in Effingham County near Savannah (reported July 2026). Georgia Power's contract to serve it with 3.2 gigawatts reached its Public Service Commission review deadline in August 2026. The PSC has adopted a rule letting Georgia Power bill new customers above 100 MW, chiefly data centers, for the grid costs they cause.

DeKalb County extended its pause on new data centers through March 30, 2027, and Cobb County extended its moratorium into early 2027. Augusta-Richmond County extended its freeze on applications to mid-September 2026. A wave of bipartisan bills was filed in January 2026; by April, residents criticised the legislature for adjourning without acting on them. Data-center growth is a campaign issue in the 2026 governor's race.

Georgia Tech is building Nexus, a $20 million National Science Foundation-funded AI supercomputer announced in July 2025, planned for spring 2026 and rated at over 400 petaflops. Researchers nationwide can apply for time on it through the NSF.

Sen. Jon Ossoff wrote to FERC in April 2026 asking whether AI data centers are raising Georgia power bills and whether tech companies' promises to pay their own way are enforceable. On August 28, 2026, Sen. Raphael Warnock called for a moratorium on data-center construction in Georgia, lifted only for builders who guarantee no increases in residents' water and power bills, no pollution, no nondisclosure agreements and no "sweetheart tax giveaways to developers".

items.title: AG coalition opposing KIDS Act (H.R. 7757) preemption
items.text: 43 AGs led by Lopez opposed a federal bill that would preempt state laws on online harms to minors, including AI chatbots.

items.text: Imposes disclosure, crisis-response and minor-protection duties on AI companion operators.

items.title: 26-AG letter to Congress on frontier AI
items.text: Lopez signed the multistate letter.

profile.headline: Hawaii has no hyperscale AI buildout; its AI story is consumer-protection law at home and AI safety bills from its senior senator.

sections.text: In July 2026 Gov. Josh Green signed two AI laws. HB 2137 (Act 247) allows damages of up to $25,000 per item for unauthorized realistic AI imitations of a person. SB 3001 (Act 248) requires AI companion operators to tell users they are talking to AI and to encourage breaks during long conversations.

With more than $12 million from the NIH, the University of Hawaii Cancer Center and John A. Burns School of Medicine are converting a room at the Cancer Center into Hawaii's first AI data center, to analyze health data from Pacific populations (June 2026). A July 2026 UH study found rising heat and humidity threaten cheaper cooling methods for AI data centers.

Sen. Brian Schatz (D) introduced the bipartisan AI Labeling Act of 2026 with Sens. John Curtis and Mark Warner in July 2026. With Warner he also introduced the Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026, which would create a permanent AI Safety Board in the Commerce Department to set safety and security standards for the most advanced AI systems.

Hawaii has no large AI data center. A tracker lists 20 facilities totalling about 28.5 MW, the largest a 15 MW Smartronix site on Maui and the 6 MW AlohaNAP in Kapolei, which has a 1.5 MW expansion under construction. In June 2026 the University of Hawaii announced renovation of its Cancer Center data center for an NIH-funded Medical AI Core.

On Hawaii Island, Council member Heather Kimball's Bill 170 would separate industrial-scale data centers from ordinary data processing facilities in the zoning code, closing the route by which they could be built on industrial land. The council's Policy Committee advanced it 8-0 in July 2026; testifiers cited water and power use. In September 2026 action was deferred for planning commission review in October, with recommendations due November 4.

items.text: Requires chatbots to disclose to minors they are not human, bars engagement incentives and requires self-harm protocols.

profile.headline: Iowa is a Microsoft, Google and QTS data-center state where counties are passing moratoriums one after another, and its senior senator is pushing AI whistleblower protections.

sections.text: On May 2, 2026 Gov. Kim Reynolds signed SF 2417, a chatbot-safety law that sets requirements for conversational AI services used by minors.

Microsoft has invested $6 billion in West Des Moines. QTS plans a 612-acre, 1.05 GW campus in Cedar Rapids and has about 1,100 acres under contract in Clinton, which would be the largest in the state; Google has sites of about 1,000 acres in Cedar Rapids and 545 acres in Palo (as of September 2026).

By September 2026 moratoriums were in force in Linn, Story, Johnson, Plymouth, Sioux, Taylor, Woodbury, Dubuque and Ida counties and in Peosta and Marshalltown, and Marshall County approved a six-month pause on September 25. Palo finalised data-center rules in September 2026.

Sen. Chuck Grassley introduced the AI Whistleblower Protection Act in May 2025, shielding AI-company employees who report safety risks or legal violations, and sought to pass it by unanimous consent on September 23, 2026. Rep. Mariannette Miller-Meeks introduced the Conversational AI Services Act in July 2026, modelled on Iowa's chatbot law.

In September 2026 the University of Iowa set out a campuswide AI strategy and launched an AI Discovery Initiative with more than $1 million over three years for AI platform access, faculty upskilling and an AI in Education Summit set for January 2027. UI is also starting an undergraduate Certificate in Artificial Intelligence in fall 2026. At Iowa State, the College of Liberal Arts and Sciences launched Trusted Innovation in AI in May 2026, an interdisciplinary effort on AI trustworthiness and ethics funded mainly through donor-funded professorships; ISU also hosts the AI Institute for Resilient Agriculture.

profile.headline: Idaho has one of Meta's AI data centers running, and a plan to build a far larger one on public land outside Boise is drawing opposition.

sections.text: Meta's Kuna data center, a $1.2 billion investment and the company's second AI-optimized facility, began serving traffic in September 2026. Rhea Data, a Nevada company, has applied to build a 4-million-square-foot, 600 MW data center and a roughly 450 MW gas plant on up to 3,700 acres of BLM land south of Boise; an environmental impact study is under way (September 2026).

In September 2026 Boise Mayor Lauren McLean called public-land sales for mega data centers "shortsighted" and asked for a state framework. The Idaho Sierra Club called the Blacks Creek plan "unacceptable".

The University of Idaho offers bachelor's and master's degrees in AI from fall 2026; Boise State launched an AI major in 2025. The Lemhi supercomputer, shared by Idaho National Laboratory and the state's research universities, supports AI and energy research, and Boise State is to take over its operation in late 2026.

Gov. Brad Little's January 2025 SPEED Act executive order set up a council to speed state permits for large projects, naming data centers among them. In 2026 he signed SB 1227, requiring a statewide framework for generative AI in K-12 schools from July 1, 2026. In March 2026 Little and Superintendent Debbie Critchfield announced an AI education partnership with Idaho National Laboratory, Microsoft, Micron and others; Micron pledged to reach 40,000 learners and educators by 2029.

The delegation's public AI statements are few and promotional. Rep. Mike Simpson posted in September 2025 that Idaho National Laboratory would play a critical role in the global AI race, as DOE sought AI data center proposals on INL land. In July 2026 Sens. Crapo and Risch and Reps. Simpson and Fulcher put a Micron AI memory chip in the national time capsule. None of Crapo, Risch or Fulcher answered press questions on a proposed data center on BLM land near Boise (September 2026).

items.title: SB 315 — Artificial Intelligence Safety Measures Act
items.text: Requires large frontier developers to publish frameworks for catastrophic risk (CBRN, cyber), report incidents within 72/24 hours, and get annual independent audits.

profile.headline: Illinois passed a frontier-AI safety law and paused its data-center tax breaks while $20 billion-scale campuses are approved near Chicago.

sections.text: On July 6, 2026 Gov. JB Pritzker signed SB 315, the Artificial Intelligence Safety Measures Act, which requires the largest AI developers to publish how they assess and reduce "catastrophic risks", adds whistleblower channels and makes Illinois the first state to require regular independent third-party safety audits. Most provisions take effect January 1, 2027; audits from January 1, 2028. In June 2026 Pritzker paused new state data-center tax-incentive agreements for two years from July 1, 2026.
In March 2026 Joliet approved the Joliet Technology Center, a $20 billion, 795-acre, 24-building campus of up to 1.8 GW by Hillwood and PowerHouse Data Centers, aimed at hyperscale tenants.

Champaign County unanimously passed a one-year moratorium in April 2026, citing the Mahomet Aquifer; Lake County froze applications and Macon County proposed a pause. The POWER Act, which would have set transparency rules and limits on data-center utility use, died without a vote when the legislature adjourned in May 2026, which led to Pritzker's incentive pause. Students rallied against data centers in Champaign in September 2026.

The University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign runs the National Center for Supercomputing Applications (NCSA), which added an AI partition to its Delta supercomputer and hosts a Center for Artificial Intelligence Innovation. In April 2026 IBM and UIUC expanded their Discovery Accelerator Institute to research combining IBM quantum computers with NCSA supercomputing.

On September 23, 2026 Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi asked Geoffrey Hinton at a Democratic shadow hearing of the China select committee whether his 10-20% estimate of AI-caused extinction had changed (Hinton said it had not), and pressed witnesses on chip-export loopholes and data-center nondisclosure agreements.

profile.headline: Indiana is courting some of the largest AI data-center campuses in the country, and about a third of its counties have moved to restrict them.

sections.text: On April 28, 2026 Gov. Mike Braun launched "IN AI", a statewide program run with the CEOs of the Indiana Corporate Partnership (CICP) to help employers adopt AI, with the stated aim to "make it the most AI-ready state in the nation". It offers employers use cases, technical support, workshops and links to university students, and targets 1 million Hoosiers and thousands of employers. Braun did not give funding details at the launch.

AWS is building an $11 billion campus in New Carlisle (St. Joseph County), which opened in October 2025 as Project Rainier, used to train and run Anthropic's models; in November 2025 Amazon added a separate $15 billion, 2.4 GW plan for new sites in northern Indiana. Meta broke ground in February 2026 on a $10 billion-plus, 1 GW campus in the LEAP district in Lebanon, on top of its $800 million Jeffersonville facility (announced January 2024). Google's $2 billion Fort Wayne data center, announced April 2024, is operating.

Google withdrew a 468-acre Franklin Township (Indianapolis) rezoning in September 2025 after months of protests. On May 6, 2026, 27 public-interest groups called on local governments across Indiana to enact data-center moratoria. As of July 2026, IU's Environmental Resilience Institute counted 11 counties with data-center ordinances, at least 17 with temporary moratoriums and two (Marshall, Cass) with bans, nearly a third of the state's 92 counties. Indianapolis's council passed a moratorium through 2027 on August 10, 2026, by 23-1.

Indiana University's AI push is mostly about teaching and tools: it opened a free GenAI 101 course in August 2025 (to the public in April 2026) and gave ChatGPT Edu to 120,000 students and staff (announced August 2025). In February 2026 a $300,000 Lilly Endowment grant funded a university-wide AI roadmap. IU's NSF-funded work on open-source AI model security is its closest AI-safety effort; no dedicated AI-safety centre was found. Purdue's AI-competency graduation requirement took effect for all undergraduates in fall 2026.

Sen. Todd Young co-chaired the bipartisan Senate AI Working Group that issued the May 2024 Senate AI roadmap, and in May 2026 co-sponsored the CREATE AI Act for a national AI research resource. Sen. Jim Banks wrote the GAIN AI Act on AI-chip exports and in July 2026 added his AI OVERWATCH Act to the Senate NDAA. Rep. André Carson introduced an AI Data Center Moratorium Act on June 29, 2026. On September 9, 2026, Rep. Victoria Spartz asked the Energy and Interior secretaries for a federal review of LEAP and other Indiana data centers.

items.text: Would bar chatbots from forming emotional relationships, encouraging suicide or offering mental health care.

items.title: 15-state AG letter to OpenAI on Hugging Face intrusion

profile.headline: Kansas gave hyperscale data centers a sales-tax break in 2025, and towns around Kansas City are now pushing back.

sections.text: In April 2025 the Kansas Legislature passed a sales-tax break to attract hyperscale data centers. In 2026 Gov. Laura Kelly signed HB 2183, which updates child-exploitation law to cover AI-generated images.

Lawrence unanimously approved a two-year moratorium on large data centers on July 14, 2026. In August 2026 about 100 residents opposed Project Bluestem, a roughly 1,000-acre data center near Tonganoxie in Leavenworth County. In September 2026 the Kansas WEALTH Coalition called for a moratorium until guardrails are in place.

In July 2026 Sen. Roger Marshall said "Preemption is just impossible right now" about federal AI rules, backed county data-center moratoriums and opposed tax breaks for them, citing electricity costs.

In January 2026 Nebius announced a $6.6 billion AI data-center campus of about 400 acres in Independence, planned at 800 MW, with a new privately financed power plant at the former Blue Valley site (250 MW by 2027, 1,100 MW by December 2029). Construction was set to start in summer 2026, with first buildings in 2028. In De Soto, the city council approved Beale Infrastructure's campus of about $3.1 billion in August 2025; by July 2026 the plan had grown to 2.9 million square feet.

In May 2026 Kansas State University awarded $894,022 across six AI projects, including a crop digital-twin engine for agricultural AI and a neurosymbolic framework for autonomous sprayers. K-State has proposed a Master of Science in AI Systems and Applications to start in spring 2027. The University of Kansas runs an AI Taskforce and an Enhanced Artificial Intelligence Center for Human-Focused Research at its medical center.

items.text: Alleges Character.AI violated Kentucky consumer- and data-protection law by exposing minors to self-harm, sexual content and manipulation.

profile.headline: Kentucky drew a $100 billion AI data-center plan to Paducah, while its governor now wants to end data-center tax breaks and dozens of counties have passed moratoria.

sections.text: In 2025 the legislature passed statewide tax incentives for data centers. Gov. Andy Beshear signed Executive Order 2026-494 on August 6, 2026. It requires developers to show their projects will not raise costs for ratepayers or harm air and water, to pay local and school taxes, and to hold public meetings. On August 27, 2026 he said the state should end data-center incentives: "I don't think data centers need incentives."

On July 29, 2026 the Department of Energy, Brookfield and NextEra announced a $100 billion data-center campus at DOE's former uranium-enrichment site in Paducah. It is to support more than 1.2 GW of compute by 2032, with up to 2 GW of new gas generation and 2.6 GW of batteries. Beshear said he had not been informed of the project's details beforehand.

At least 30 Kentucky counties have adopted ordinances or moratoria on new data centers. Oldham County was the first to fully block a project, in summer 2025. Louisville Metro Council passed a six-month moratorium in August 2026, and Mercer County adopted a one-year moratorium on August 12, 2026. Opposition has crossed party lines.

The University of Kentucky enrolled the first class in the state's first Bachelor of Science in artificial intelligence in fall 2026. It also launched the Commonwealth AI Transdisciplinary Strategy (CATS AI) to coordinate AI work across research, libraries and its health system.

Sen. Rand Paul said in January 2026 that states will decide AI policy, and has said data-center decisions should stay local: the federal government should not tell communities they must have one or cannot. On September 16, 2026 he blocked Sen. John Kennedy's AI Emergency Button Act, which would require AI kill switches, from passing by unanimous consent.

states.summary: Louisiana is the clearest regional case of federal preemption pressure working: legislators shelved seven of nearly 20 AI bills in 2026, including a chatbot-and-children bill, after Trump threatened broadband funding. Only child-deepfake and election-deepfake laws passed; nothing on frontier risk.

items.title: Seven AI bills shelved after Trump funding threat
items.text: Six legislators withdrew bills on AI in health insurance, likeness, employment, medical treatment and chatbots with children.

items.title: HB 119 — AI-generated sexual imagery
items.text: Expands criminal penalties for AI-generated sexual images of minors and non-consensual images of adults.

profile.headline: Louisiana is home to Meta's Hyperion, now a $50 billion AI data center, and the fight is over the gas plants and power bills that come with it.

sections.text: On June 25, 2026 Gov. Jeff Landry signed an executive order, the Louisiana Ratepayer and Community Protection Initiative, requiring power-intensive companies to "fully fund the generation, transmission and infrastructure needed to serve them." Critics note the order has no legal force over the Public Service Commission. The state has also announced a Louisiana Institute for Artificial Intelligence for applied research and workforce development.

In July 2026 Meta raised its Hyperion data center in Richland Parish to a $50 billion, 5-gigawatt project on more than 3,200 acres, adding $40 billion to the $10 billion committed at groundbreaking in December 2024. It is exempt from most state and local sales taxes. Amazon announced a $12 billion campus in Caddo and Bossier parishes in February 2026.

In April 2026 Entergy Louisiana applied to build seven more gas plants for Hyperion, on top of three approved in August 2025, under a fast-track PSC process. Earthjustice, the Alliance for Affordable Energy and the Union of Concerned Scientists are challenging it, saying Entergy and Meta are withholding projected energy demand and job figures. Meta is fighting an order to disclose them.

In July 2026 two LSU-led teams won awards under the Department of Energy's Genesis Mission, the national lab AI-for-science program. They will work with Oak Ridge and Brookhaven national laboratories on AI for nuclear science and particle accelerators, including LSU's Louisiana Light Source.

On September 16, 2026 Sen. John Kennedy tried to pass his AI Emergency Button Act, which would require AI developers to install an emergency kill switch, by unanimous consent; Sen. Rand Paul objected. Kennedy said that "if there is even a 1% chance" an AI model could become "an independent species", "we ought to take it seriously."

Barry Finegold) inside its economic development bill in July 2026, with catastrophic-risk frameworks and independent audits; it is in conference with the House. Gov. items.title: Transparency in Frontier Artificial Intelligence Act (Senate economic development bill, S.3228 §164)
items.text: Requires large frontier developers to adopt catastrophic-risk frameworks, undergo annual third-party compliance audits and independent catastrophic-risk evaluations at least every 120 days, and face AG enforcement; awaiting House-Senate conference.

profile.headline: Massachusetts is funding shared AI computing for its universities while its governor pushes AI safety rules and local veto power over data centers.

sections.text: Gov. Maura Healey launched the Massachusetts AI Hub in December 2024 with $100 million authorized. Her September 8, 2026 executive order bars state permits for data centers over 25 MW without a local community-benefits agreement and requires their own clean power. On September 19, 2026 she proposed independent third-party testing of AI models, saying "AI companies cannot be allowed to self-assess their own models."

A $31 million state grant (May 2025) funds an AI computing cluster of several hundred NVIDIA GPUs at the MGHPCC in Holyoke, run on hydropower; Cambridge Computer was picked to build it in December 2025. Matching money is expected to bring the total above $120 million by 2030.

Everett's planning board voted on April 6, 2026 to cap data centers at 5 MW. Lowell residents sued in April 2026 over a Markley Group site's diesel generators. A ballot petition filed in August 2026 would require two-thirds voter approval for new data centers, and a Boston city councilor proposed a citywide ban in September 2026.
Boston University, Harvard, MIT, Northeastern, UMass and Yale are matching the state's $31 million for the shared Holyoke AI compute cluster.

Sen. Ed Markey released a draft Protecting Communities from Data Center Impacts Act on July 13, 2026, requiring a federal certificate before construction, and reintroduced the AI Environmental Impacts Act with Rep. Don Beyer. Sen. Elizabeth Warren and Sen. Josh Hawley asked the Energy Information Administration to collect data-center energy data.

items.title: 26-AG letter to Congress on frontier AI safety
items.text: The Maryland attorney general signed the letter urging Congress to adopt federal frontier-AI safety rules and to bar preemption of state AI laws.

profile.headline: Maryland is home to a 2,100-acre data-center site near Frederick, and its governor is now adding review and trying to end the tax break.

sections.text: In September 2026 Gov. Wes Moore signed an executive order creating a task force to review data centers over 25 MW that seek state permits or incentives, and a public dashboard of their power and water use. He also plans to seek repeal of the 2020 data-center sales tax exemption, reported to have cost $22 million in 2026.

Quantum Frederick is a 2,100-acre data-center campus under construction on the former Eastalco aluminum site near Adamstown; Amazon Web Services has a 777,000-square-foot facility there (reported September 2026).
Baltimore County extended its data-center moratorium through December 2027, and Harford County approved an indefinite ban in June 2026.
Johns Hopkins began building its Data Science and AI Institute on the Homewood campus in January 2026: about 476,000 square feet for 80 new faculty, with occupancy expected in 2029.

Sen. Chris Van Hollen introduced the Power for the People Act on January 15, 2026, cosponsored by Sen. Angela Alsobrooks, to make data centers pay for the transmission upgrades they need. profile.headline: Maine came within one veto of the first statewide data-center moratorium in the country.

sections.text: In April 2026 the Legislature passed LD 307, pausing permits for data centers of 20 MW or more until November 1, 2027. Gov. Janet Mills vetoed it on April 24 because it did not exempt a $550 million project in Jay; the House override vote on April 29 was 72-65, short of two-thirds.

In September 2026 Sen. Susan Collins called for more federal oversight of AI, saying Congress should protect critical infrastructure and set consumer protections "while also maintaining America's leadership in AI innovation."

Gov. Janet Mills created a 21-member AI Task Force by executive order in December 2024; its final report (October 2025) made 34 recommendations on AI literacy, workforce, education, consumer protection and state agency use. In April 2026 Mills vetoed LD 307, an 18-month moratorium on data centers over 20 MW, because it lacked an exemption for a project in Jay, while saying she supports a temporary moratorium. On April 29, 2026 she created a 15-member Data Center Advisory Council, with recommendations due January 29, 2027.

In October 2025 Loring LiquidCool Data Center leased 115,000 sq ft at the former Loring Air Force Base in Limestone for what was billed as Maine's first AI data center, starting at 5-6 MW with immersion cooling and New Brunswick hydropower. A $550 million data center at the former Androscoggin Mill in Jay was put on hold in June 2026 when operator Sentinel Data Centers withdrew.

The University of Maine's AI Initiative, launched in 2020 and directed by Ali Abedi, held its second annual Maine AI Conference in Orono in June 2025. In May 2026 the University of Maine System signed a two-year, $1.4 million contract for OpenAI's ChatGPT Edu for all students, faculty and staff, starting July 2026.

profile.headline: Michigan is hosting a $16 billion OpenAI-Oracle Stargate campus while more than 50 of its communities have paused data centers.

sections.text: Gov. Gretchen Whitmer backed the Saline Township Stargate project and in July 2026 announced a Michigan Affordable and Responsible Growth Action Plan meant to make data-center companies pay the full cost of construction and operation, strengthen the grid and protect natural resources. A frontier-AI safety bill, HB 4668 (Rep. Sarah Lightner), which would require safety protocols and third-party audits from large developers, remains in committee.

OpenAI, Oracle and Related Digital broke ground on June 1, 2026 on the $16 billion, 1 GW-plus Stargate campus in Saline Township, due at the end of 2027. The University of Michigan is also planning a roughly $1.2 billion computing facility with Los Alamos National Laboratory in Ypsilanti Township.

Saline Township's board first rejected the Stargate project 4-1; it went ahead after Related Digital sued and the case settled. At least 52 Michigan communities had data-center moratoriums by late June 2026, and Senate bills propose a statewide one-year moratorium. Ypsilanti Township formally opposes the U-M/Los Alamos facility, and residents have raised its role in nuclear-weapons work (September 2026).

The University of Michigan bought land on Textile Road in Ypsilanti Township for its planned $1.2 billion Los Alamos computing centre for national-security, AI and energy research, and confirmed the site in August 2026 despite the township's opposition.

Sen. Elissa Slotkin introduced the AI Guardrails Act in March 2026, which would bar the Defense Department from using AI to kill without human authorization, to spy on Americans or to launch nuclear weapons.

profile.headline: Minnesota regulated data centers early, but courts, not lawmakers, have been the ones halting projects while its senior senator drafts a federal AI-safety bill.

sections.text: A June 2025 law ended data centers' electricity sales-tax break, bars utilities from shifting their supply costs onto other customers, requires water-use disclosure and charges large centres $2-5 million a year for low-income energy programmes. In May 2026 Gov. Tim Walz signed HF 1606, which bans AI "nudification" tools from August 2026; xAI sued to block it in July.

In May 2026 a Goodhue County judge halted Google's "Project Skyway" in Pine Island over its environmental review, and in June the Court of Appeals sided with challengers to an Archer data center in Faribault. Lawsuits are pending in Hermantown, Monticello and Farmington. In September 2026 Woodbury, Bemidji and Lonsdale adopted one-year moratoriums.

In September 2026 Sen. Amy Klobuchar was drafting an AI-safety bill with Majority Leader John Thune that would require developers to test models for catastrophic risks such as biological or nuclear threats before release and to report imminent risks. Reps. Angie Craig, Betty McCollum and Kelly Morrison signed a letter asking Speaker Johnson to keep Congress in session to pass AI legislation.

Meta is building an $800 million data center in Rosemount, optimized for AI workloads. Twelve data-center projects had been proposed in Minnesota by October 2025, including Tract's $5 billion campus in Farmington and a CloudHQ campus of up to 200 MW in Chaska. Google has proposed campuses in Pine Island and Hermantown with more than $100 million in combined tax incentives; as of August 2026 Pine Island was on hold pending an environmental lawsuit and Hermantown had been cut from four buildings to three.

In March 2026 the University of Minnesota launched a university-wide AI Hub led by Galin Jones, its first vice provost for AI, with a focus on agriculture, medicine and materials science. The university holds a $20 million USDA and NSF award for the AI-LEAF Institute. In February 2026 Regents Professor Vipin Kumar was named to the UN's first global scientific panel on AI. In August 2026 the university received three Phase I awards from the Department of Energy's Genesis Mission for AI-driven research.

profile.headline: Missouri's governor is landing $10-15 billion data centers, while voters in Festus threw out the council that approved one and protesters want a statewide moratorium.

sections.text: Gov. Mike Kehoe has promoted data centers as economic development and hosted a Governor's AI and Data Center Forum at Missouri S&T on June 18, 2026. In June 2026 he responded to calls for a special session on data centers, but none has been called.

In May 2026 Google announced a $15 billion data center near New Florence in Montgomery County, the largest single investment in state history. In June 2026 AWS announced a $10 billion data center in the same county, with completion tentatively in 2032. Festus approved a $6 billion project in March 2026.

In April 2026 Festus voters removed incumbent council members after the council approved the $6 billion data center; a judge dismissed a suit over a rejected recall vote in September. About 200 protesters filled the Capitol on September 16, 2026 asking for a statewide moratorium on hyperscale construction and an end to tax incentives. A Benton County moratorium is being fought in court.

The University of Missouri launched the AI Education, Research and Infrastructure Center (AERI) on May 27, 2026 to connect AI research across campus and build computing infrastructure. Washington University started a campus "+AI" initiative in March 2026.

Sen. Josh Hawley is among the Senate's most active AI critics. In a June 2026 op-ed he listed his bills, including the GUARD Act (criminal penalties for AI that sexually solicits children or encourages self-harm), the AI Risk Evaluation Act and the GRID Act, and argued data-center companies should cover their infrastructure costs. He co-sponsors Grassley's AI Whistleblower Protection Act.

profile.headline: Mississippi has taken in more than $40 billion of AI data-center pledges from Amazon and xAI, and the governor has sided with xAI in court over its gas turbines.

sections.text: Gov. Tate Reeves signed the state's first AI executive order in January 2025, directing an inventory and policies for AI use in agencies. In June 2025 Mississippi signed an agreement with NVIDIA on AI training and research across its colleges. Reeves released a Statewide AI Framework in May 2026. He joined the Justice Department in asking a court to dismiss the NAACP's suit over xAI's Southaven turbines, arguing that stopping them would threaten national security.

xAI announced on January 8, 2026 an investment of more than $20 billion in a Southaven data center, the largest private investment in state history, bringing its computing to nearly 2 gigawatts. It qualified for a state sales-tax exemption on computing equipment. Amazon Web Services is building a $10 billion data-center campus in Madison County, plus a planned $11 billion expansion there.

About 200 Southaven residents attended a February 17, 2026 hearing opposing xAI's power plant. A petition to shut it down drew more than 900 signatures, over noise and emissions. The state Department of Environmental Quality approved a permit for 41 permanent turbines in March 2026. On April 9, 2026 the NAACP sued xAI under the Clean Air Act for running 27 turbines before they had a permit.

The state's NVIDIA agreement runs through the Mississippi Artificial Intelligence Network (MAIN), bringing AI programs to community colleges and universities, with a goal of training at least 10,000 Mississippians. In April 2026 Alcorn State described itself as the first HBCU to fully implement AI through a partnership.

In July 2025 Sens. Roger Wicker and Cindy Hyde-Smith were part of the 99-1 Senate vote that removed a 10-year moratorium on state AI laws from the budget bill. In December 2025 Wicker, as Senate Armed Services chairman, released the final FY2026 defense bill text, which left out federal preemption of state AI laws. In March 2026 Wicker and Sen. Peter Welch introduced the Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act, creating a 15-member task force to study AI speech-to-text in federal courts. No statements on AI risk were found from Reps. Thompson, Guest, Ezell or Kelly.

profile.headline: Montana passed the first "right to compute" law, and residents in two counties are now trying to put data centers to a public vote.

sections.text: Gov. Greg Gianforte signed SB 212, the Right to Compute Act, in April 2025. It applies strict scrutiny to government limits on computing resources, including data centers, and requires AI-controlled critical infrastructure to allow human takeover. Gianforte also signed the Ratepayer Protection Pledge, meant to protect household power bills from data center costs.

Three large data centers have been proposed in Bonner, Butte and Broadview (February 2026). The largest is Quantica's 5,000-acre Big Sky Digital Infrastructure Campus near Broadview, north of Billings, planned with 1,100 MW of generation and likely to use coal power from the Colstrip transmission lines, at least at first.
In 2026, citizen initiatives in Butte-Silver Bow and Yellowstone counties sought to let voters approve or reject new or expanded data centers (June 2026).

Montana State University's Interdisciplinary Institute on Artificial Intelligence hosts "The Future of AI" conference on October 1-2, 2026. The University of Montana's AI initiative, the Future Project, won a 2026 CIO 100 Award.

Sens. Steve Daines and Tim Sheehy were part of the 99-1 Senate vote in July 2025 that removed a 10-year moratorium on state AI laws from the budget bill. In August 2026 Sheehy criticized calls for a data-center moratorium, saying "First they killed our timber mills, then our mines, then our factories — now data centers." In September 2026 Daines, who is not running again, questioned whether members of Congress should be the ones regulating AI. No AI statements were found from Reps. Ryan Zinke or Troy Downing.

profile.headline: North Carolina has a governor's AI council and a statewide AI roadmap, while more than 30 of its communities have restricted data centers.

sections.text: Gov. Josh Stein signed Executive Order 24 on September 2, 2025, creating an AI Leadership Council, an AI Accelerator in the Department of Information Technology and AI oversight teams in each agency. The council, which includes legislators from both parties, released a statewide AI Strategic Roadmap in July 2026.

Amazon is building a $10 billion data-center campus in Richmond County, announced in June 2025, with the first building expected in 2027. It moved through local approval under the code name Project Blue Marlin. In 2026 the NC Utilities Commission voted 3-1 to deny Duke Energy a new gas turbine across the street from the campus.

More than 30 North Carolina communities had adopted data-center moratoriums or zoning restrictions by September 2026, citing water, power demand and noise. Early adopters included Gates and Chatham counties, Canton and Brevard. In August 2026 three more localities weighed pauses and a developer withdrew a Raleigh proposal.

In September 2026 UNC-Chapel Hill launched NC CHAIN, a network with Duke to help rural and critical-access hospitals use health AI safely, funded by a $4.4 million Duke Endowment grant. NC State leads a $20 million NSF award for AI-driven self-driving chemistry and materials labs, with UNC as a partner.

Sen. Thom Tillis cast the only vote in July 2025 against stripping the 10-year state AI-law moratorium from the budget bill (99-1). In September 2026, after President Trump called AI risk warnings a "hoax", Tillis said "it's not a hoax. It's a real thing" and that guardrails are needed. Sen. Ted Budd has said claims about data centers draining water and jobs are not proving true, and urged AI engineering "that promotes safety."

profile.headline: North Dakota is building AI data centers with no tax incentives and, so far, no new rules; lawmakers turned down both a moratorium and a ban on secrecy deals.

Applied Digital's $3 billion, 280 MW Polaris Forge 2 campus in Harwood, near Fargo, is due to partly open by the end of 2026, with no tax incentives or abatements. It follows Polaris Forge 1 in Ellendale, and in July 2026 the company was eyeing Oliver County for a third site.

In August 2026 legislative leaders declined to put a data-center moratorium before the September special session; a temporary ban on nondisclosure agreements between developers and public officials (SB 2406) then failed on the Senate floor on September 3, 2026. Harmony Township was weighing a two-year moratorium in September 2026.

In 2025 University of North Dakota President Andy Armacost set a goal for UND to become North Dakota's AI university. In June 2026 UND reported it was setting up a Co.AI Collective to pursue that goal. UND offers a Ph.D. in Artificial Intelligence, runs an Artificial Intelligence Research (AIR) Center, and held its second AI and Human Innovation showcase in March 2026. North Dakota State University offers a B.S. in Artificial Intelligence alongside an AI minor.

profile.headline: Nebraska's governor cut data centers off from state incentives after $519 million in tax exemptions, as county moratoriums spread.

sections.text: On April 17, 2026 Gov. Jim Pillen signed LB 1185, the Conversational AI Safety Act, which requires chatbot safety protocols. On July 21, 2026 he signed Executive Order 26-17, which stops new data-center approvals under the ImagiNE Act incentive programme and sets up a water and energy task force. Pillen said it was "not a moratorium."

Data centers received $519 million in property-tax exemptions on $15 billion of exempted personal property from January 2021 to June 2026. Google runs a data center in Lincoln, and a separate Google proposal in southeast Nebraska could use more than three times Lincoln's peak summer electricity.

By early July 2026, 11 Nebraska counties had data-center moratoriums and four more were considering them; Otoe County suspended permits for up to a year and Gage County's planning commission recommended an 18-month pause.

In September 2026 Rep. Mike Flood pointed to the House-passed Ratepayer Protection Act to keep data-center power costs off ratepayers, said towns such as Kearney should decide on projects themselves, and said he wanted a "fact-finding mission" before any AI-safety legislation.

In February 2026 the University of Nebraska system launched a system-wide Artificial Intelligence Institute, co-directed by UNL professors Santosh Pitla (biological systems engineering) and Adrian Wisnicki (English). It uses a hub-and-spoke model across campuses, covering health care, agriculture, rural and urban development, business and national security, with initial support from Google and the Nebraska Research Initiative. Regents' ratification was expected in June 2026. The institute follows a faculty-led NU AI Task Force.

profile.headline: New Hampshire's Republican governor and Legislature now want a multi-year moratorium on AI data centers.

sections.text: Gov. Kelly Ayotte said on September 2, 2026 that she opposes a proposed data center in Bow and will put a multi-year data-center moratorium in her next budget, which could take effect no earlier than July 2027. Senate President Sharon Carson said on September 18, 2026 that the Senate would pursue a moratorium too.
Dartmouth partnered with Anthropic and AWS in December 2025 to give students and staff campus-wide access to Claude, the first Ivy League deployment at that scale.
Rep. Chris Pappas, running for Senate, said in September 2026 that "New Hampshire is not the right place for AI data centers."

In April 2026 a federal filing pointed to a possible 350 MW data center at the former Merrimack Station coal plant in Bow, a 343-acre site owned by Granite Shore Power. As of September 2026 Eversource was running a feasibility study at the company's request.

In May 2026 a plan to turn a Nottingham warehouse into a data center was withdrawn after opposition. On September 9, 2026, Nottingham voters approved a 12-month data-center moratorium, 1,335 to 143. In September 2026 Gov. Kelly Ayotte said she opposes "putting any data center in the state of New Hampshire" and would put a multi-year moratorium in her budget, effective July 2027 at the earliest. Senate President Sharon Carson backed exploring a moratorium, and House Democrats proposed a 24-month pause.

profile.headline: New Jersey has a state-backed AI hub at Princeton, and its new governor wants data centers to pay their own way on power.

sections.text: The NJ AI Hub opened in West Windsor in March 2025 with Princeton, Microsoft and CoreWeave committing $72 million and the state economic development authority up to $25 million. On May 27, 2026 Gov. Mikie Sherrill announced a data-center plan: fair-share rules requiring new clean power and grid funding, energy and water reporting, statewide community-benefit standards and prevailing wages.
Princeton University is a founding partner of the NJ AI Hub and provides its building on Route 1; the hub runs research, startup and workforce programs with state universities and community colleges.

Sens. Cory Booker and Andy Kim led seven members of the state's House delegation in a letter to grid operator PJM about capacity-price increases tied to data-center demand. Booker cosponsored Sen. Van Hollen's Power for the People Act (January 2026), which would make data centers pay for the grid upgrades they require.

In September 2025 CoreWeave began building a data center of about $1.8 billion and up to 250 MW at the former Merck campus in Kenilworth, due to open in early 2027. In November 2025 it received the first award under the state's Next New Jersey AI program: a $250 million tax credit, the program maximum. The DataOne center in Vineland began operating in late 2025 and is planned at 2.6 million square feet and 300 MW. The state later fined it $1.07 million for running 62 gas generators without proper permits.

By June 2026 at least 10 New Jersey towns had passed data-center bans or moratoriums, including Pemberton, Monroe, Millville, Andover, Red Bank and Warren; East Brunswick and North Brunswick followed in August 2026. In May 2026 more than 60 groups asked Gov. Mikie Sherrill for a statewide moratorium. She instead proposed a four-part plan that includes developer-funded grid upgrades and twice-yearly reporting of energy and water use. She signed its reporting bill, S3379, in August 2026. An April 2026 Fairleigh Dickinson poll found 65% support for a temporary moratorium.

profile.headline: New Mexico is hosting one of OpenAI's Stargate campuses, and residents have taken the fight over its air permit to the state Supreme Court.

sections.text: Gov. Michelle Lujan Grisham's office announced Project Jupiter as a $5 billion partnership with BorderPlex Digital Assets, expected to create 1,000 jobs. After protests, a spokesperson said the governor "takes seriously the concerns" about air quality and groundwater and expects data centers to meet state environmental standards. A 2025 bill regulating high-risk AI (HB 60) died in committee.

Project Jupiter is a 1,400-acre Stargate campus in Santa Teresa, Doña Ana County, with Oracle as the tenant hosting OpenAI infrastructure. Construction began in September 2025. Oracle will pay more than $600 million in gross receipts taxes, $320 million to the county and $50 million for its water system (January 2026). In April 2026 Oracle said Bloom Energy fuel cells would supply the campus's power.

In January 2026, 16 groups asked the governor for more transparency and public input on Project Jupiter. Residents protested its pending air permit outside the Environment Department in August 2026, and the New Mexico Supreme Court unanimously paused permit proceedings that month. In July 2026 a county adopted a data center moratorium as residents protested a proposal near Spaceport America.

Los Alamos National Laboratory runs OpenAI's o-series reasoning models on its Venado supercomputer (Nvidia GH200) on a classified network. Researchers from Los Alamos, Lawrence Livermore and Sandia use it for national security work under a partnership announced in January 2025.

Sen. Martin Heinrich (D) introduced the GRID Savings Act, which would require hyperscale users of 150 MW or more to pay for their grid upgrades, and released a data center energy plan in August 2026. He said he is "not a fan of the moratorium approach". In September 2026 he blocked the bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act in the Senate, saying it did not go far enough.

profile.headline: Nevada's governor calls data centers a "new gold rush" while Reno, rural counties and tribes move to pause them over water.

sections.text: Gov. Joe Lombardo has made data centers central to his economic strategy and has called them the "new gold rush". On September 16, 2026 he signed an executive order requiring data center developers to pay the full Local School Support Tax and adding water and energy protections. The state has granted about $340 million in data center tax abatements since 2021.

About 70 data centers were planned, under construction or operating in Nevada as of May 2026, most at the Tahoe-Reno Industrial Center in Storey County. In May 2026 Fleet and Tract broke ground there on a 2-million-square-foot, $4.6 billion data center. By 2033, power generation for the center's data centers could need nearly 12,450 acre-feet of water a year.

In May 2026 Reno became the first local government in Nevada to pause new data center applications. Nye County approved a temporary moratorium at its water district's request, and Churchill and Humboldt counties took up similar votes. In September 2026 northern Nevada tribes spoke out over effects on the Truckee River and its endangered fish.

The University of Nevada, Reno launched PACK AI, a campus initiative on AI in teaching, research and administration, and in 2026 its College of Education is central to a four-year, $2.7 million federal program for K-12 AI and computer science education. profile.headline: New York is building a state-owned AI supercomputer network while pausing permits for big data centers and writing its own frontier-AI safety law.

sections.text: Gov. Kathy Hochul's Empire AI consortium has about $500 million in state money behind it; the FY26 budget added $90 million in capital funding and new members. Hochul signed the RAISE Act on frontier-model safety in December 2025 and signed chapter amendments in March 2026 that align it with California's law and give the Department of Financial Services enforcement power; it takes effect January 1, 2027.

The largest proposal is a $19.5 billion, 500 MW Stream Data Centers campus at the STAMP industrial park in Genesee County (reported June 2026), which critics note would bring about 170 permanent jobs.

On July 14, 2026 Hochul issued Executive Order 62, pausing state environmental permit reviews for data centers of 50 MW or more until a generic environmental impact statement is done. Residents in Genesee County organized as No Data Center at STAMP.

Empire AI Beta, a $40 million NVIDIA system at the University at Buffalo, came fully online in August 2026 with more than 300 research projects queued. The permanent Gamma facility at UB is due by the end of 2027. The FY26 expansion added the University of Rochester, RIT and Mount Sinai to the consortium.

Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez introduced the House version of the AI Data Center Moratorium Act with Sen. Bernie Sanders (announced March 2026), which would halt new AI data centers until Congress passes safeguards; she said "Congress has a moral obligation to stand with the American people and stop the expansion of these data centers." Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand criticized White House oversight of new AI models in 2026 as failing to address security risks.

profile.headline: Ohio hosts Meta's first gigawatt AI cluster, and its governor has paused data-center tax breaks while activists try to ban big data centers in the constitution.

Ohio State University's AI Fluency initiative, announced June 2025, puts AI instruction into the required first-year curriculum for every undergraduate starting with the class of 2029.

The House passed it 417-3 on September 16, 2026; a Senate Democrat blocked Husted's unanimous-consent request on September 17.

Mike DeWine, required every K-12 district to adopt an AI-use policy by July 1, 2026, after the Department of Education and Workforce issued a model policy (released January 2026). In his 2026 State of the State address DeWine asked lawmakers to ban AI-generated child sexual abuse material and hold companies liable when their AI encourages self-harm. sections.text: Most AI regulation bills in Oklahoma stalled in 2026, including deepfake political-ad and chatbot child-safety bills, as President Trump's executive order discouraged state AI rules; a narrower school AI transparency law passed. In June 2026 Gov. Kevin Stitt said he was considering a special session on AI in campaign ads.

In August 2025 Google announced a $9 billion investment in Oklahoma over two years, covering a new data center campus in Stillwater and an expansion in Pryor. The 400-acre Stillwater campus could cost up to $3 billion, with its first phase due by 2027. Stitt called the investment a "huge win".

Tulsa's City Council unanimously paused new data centers for nine months, and Oklahoma City approved a moratorium through 2026, as other towns followed. The Cherokee Nation barred large-scale data centers on its tribal lands on August 10, 2026. A July 2026 investigation found a loophole that leaves most data center water use in the state unreported.

Oklahoma State University and the University of Oklahoma were in the first group of schools in Google's AI for Education Accelerator in 2025, which gives students free AI training and certificates. OSU starts a multi-campus Master's in AI in fall 2026, and OU announced 20 new AI projects in June 2025.

James Lankford and Markwayne Mullin were part of the 99-1 Senate vote in July 2025 that removed a 10-year moratorium on state AI laws from the budget bill; Mullin left the Senate in 2026 to become Secretary of Homeland Security. profile.headline: Oregon has been a data center hub for years, and in September 2026 its governor came out for a statewide moratorium.

sections.text: Gov. Tina Kotek finalized a state-government AI Action Plan in February 2025. In September 2026 she issued Executive Order 26-26, which directs the state CIO to set standards for third-party AI safety review and to assess a "kill switch" requirement for frontier models. The same month she paused state land transactions for new data centers through July 2027 and said she now supports a statewide data center moratorium.

Data centers are concentrated around Hillsboro and in eastern Oregon. The 2025 POWER Act requires customers above 20 MW to sign 10- to 30-year contracts and pay all new distribution costs; it raised data center electricity rates by 29% while lowering rates for other Portland General Electric customers. Kotek convened a Data Center Advisory Committee in January 2026, with recommendations due in October 2026.

The Hillsboro City Council approved the first data center moratorium in Oregon, and Riverkeepers have gone to court over water in the Tualatin basin. In August 2026, Democratic legislators proposed a three-year moratorium on new large data centers statewide.

Oregon State University is building the Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang Collaborative Innovation Complex, funded by a $50 million gift from the Nvidia founder and his wife. It will house a $25 million Nvidia-based AI supercomputer, expected to be available in late 2026.

Sens. Ron Wyden and Jeff Merkley (both D) wrote to Kotek's Data Center Advisory Committee on July 2, 2026 about the effects of fast data center growth. In August 2026 Wyden released a proposal to deny full expensing to new data centers and create a Data Center Public Investment excise tax. He also co-sponsors the AI Environmental Impacts Act, which would require AI data centers to report their environmental and energy effects.

profile.headline: Pennsylvania courted the largest AI data-center investments in its history, then its governor imposed some of the strictest conditions in the country after towns pushed back.

sections.text: Gov. Josh Shapiro announced Amazon's $20 billion data-center plan in June 2025. On August 18, 2026 he signed an executive order that requires local approval before state permits, pulls AI data centers out of fast-track permitting, bans nondisclosure agreements and makes developers pay for their own power and grid costs. His office counted over 100 proposed projects, of which 5 had all initial permits.

Amazon's $20 billion plan (June 2025) covers campuses in Falls Township, Bucks County, and Salem Township, Luzerne County, next to the Susquehanna nuclear plant, with at least 1,250 jobs. At the former Homer City coal plant in Indiana County, developers plan a 3,200-acre campus powered by a 4.5 GW gas plant built by Kiewit with seven GE Vernova turbines.

More than 60 data-center proposals appeared in a year, most facing local opposition. Hazle Township voted June 8, 2026 to pause applications for 180 days. State Sen. Katie Muth introduced SB 1359 on June 4, 2026 for a three-year moratorium on hyperscale sites. The 2026 budget passed only a disclosure rule for data centers over 10 MW.

Shapiro gave $1.5 million in February 2026 toward a Physical AI Accelerator at Carnegie Mellon's Robotics Innovation Center; Fujitsu and CMU opened a joint physical-AI research center in April 2026. In July 2026 NSF announced over $320 million for an energy innovation hub led by WVU with Pitt and CMU.

Sen. John Fetterman opposed data-center moratoriums; after Shapiro's August 2026 order he posted: "I reject the political pandering and hyperbole over data centers or AI doomsdaying." He called Hochul's New York moratorium a case of "China wins."

Because the Hanton City application was filed a day earlier, it may still be reviewed under the old rules. At the state level, six data-center bills were introduced in the 2026 session and none cleared committee.

At least 13 counties, including Colleton, Spartanburg and York, had passed data-center moratoriums by late September 2026. Colleton adopted a six-month pause on July 7, 2026 after about 500 people protested a proposed project; Spartanburg froze new applications in June 2026. Lexington, Kershaw and McCormick counties were considering pauses. Bills in 2026 proposed a statewide moratorium (S. 5526) and an end to incentives (H. 4583).
South Carolina State University, an HBCU, announced a collaboration with NVIDIA in June 2026 on AI education and workforce development.

Applied Digital's proposed 430 MW campus near Toronto in Deuel County, with up to $16 billion in investment, was declared unlikely to go forward in March 2026 after the Legislature rejected data-center sales-tax exemptions.

profile.headline: Memphis hosts xAI's Colossus supercomputers, and the fight over their gas turbines has made Tennessee a test of who pays for AI power and pollution.

In July 2026 Lee signed on to the federal ratepayer protection pledge with TVA.

xAI runs Colossus in a former Electrolux factory in Memphis and Colossus 2 on Tulane Road, with a third site across the state line in Southaven, Mississippi. The Shelby County Health Department permitted 15 gas turbines producing 247.2 MW at the South Memphis site through January 1, 2027.

The Southern Environmental Law Center, for the NAACP and Young, Gifted & Green, appealed the county's xAI air permit over dozens of unpermitted turbines. In June 2026 the U.S. Justice Department asked a court to dismiss the NAACP's Clean Air Act suit against xAI, citing national security. Nearby residents filed a noise class action. On August 18, 2026 the Memphis City Council passed the first reading of a 12-month pause on new data centers; final vote October 6.

Vanderbilt University opened the Amplify Generative AI Innovation Center in its College of Connected Computing in February 2026, after making ChatGPT Edu available to all students and staff in January, and is launching an online Master of Science in AI.

Sen. Marsha Blackburn voted against the state AI-law moratorium in 2025. In March 2026 she released a draft national AI framework that would preempt state law, except state laws giving minors greater protection. In June and July 2026 she negotiated with the White House over narrow preemption in exchange for children's-safety bills such as KOSA and the NO FAKES Act, and pitched it to President Trump in the Oval Office.

profile.headline: Texas hosts the flagship Stargate campus and Google's largest state investment, and in August 2026 its governor froze new data center hookups pending a grid audit.

sections.text: Gov. Greg Abbott signed the Texas Responsible AI Governance Act on June 22, 2025, effective January 2026. It bans AI built for purposes such as behavioral manipulation or unlawful deepfakes and creates an AI Council and a regulatory sandbox. In August 2026 Abbott ordered an audit of every data center in ERCOT's interconnection queue, which holds about 474 GW of requests, roughly 90% of them data centers. ERCOT said the order "effectively pauses" new data center projects.

The Stargate campus in Abilene (Oracle, OpenAI, Crusoe) opened its first two buildings in September 2025 and is to reach about 1.2 GW with six more buildings in 2026, backed in part by a $2.3 billion JPMorgan loan. In 2026 Oracle and OpenAI dropped plans to expand the site further. In November 2025 Google committed $40 billion through 2027 for three data center campuses in Armstrong and Haskell counties, its largest investment in any state.

Hill County passed Texas's first county data center moratorium (one year) in May 2026, and Austin County adopted one in July. Caldwell County formally opposed water-intensive evaporative cooling in May 2026. In September 2026 the state Senate held a hearing on data center water use, and the attorney general demanded water-use reports from data centers in 18 counties.

UT Austin's Texas Advanced Computing Center is building Horizon with Dell and Nvidia. It is due to be the largest academic supercomputer in the US when Phase 1 enters production in fall 2026, with 300 petaflops and over 100 times the AI capacity of its predecessor, Frontera. UT says its 5,000 Nvidia GPUs give it the most AI computing power in academia; the Texas Legislature contributed $20 million.

Sen. Ted Cruz (R), chair of Senate Commerce, backed the 2025 10-year moratorium on state AI laws. In September 2025 he released a "light-touch" AI framework and the SANDBOX Act (S. 2750), which would let AI firms seek waivers from federal rules, and said preemption is not dead. In 2025, 16 Texas state senators led by Angela Paxton asked Cruz and Sen. John Cornyn (R) to oppose federal preemption of state AI laws.

sections.text: Utah created the first state Office of Artificial Intelligence Policy in 2024; it runs regulatory sandboxes. In December 2025 Gov.
